strings: The software was the surface
An operations manager at a 60-person home-services business is told to choose between two rostering platforms before the current contract expires.
Use Frame Free in this PDF. Ask me one question at a time.
Find the question behind the question
The first three moves make the decision explicit, expose the deeper issue and reopen the option set.
Separate evidence from assumption
The final three moves identify the belief carrying the decision, test what has been treated as fixed and make the evidence state visible.
Framed is not decided
The decision and trigger
What exactly are you deciding, and what made it live now?
The decision underneath
If the immediate choice disappeared, what larger question would remain?
The missing option
Which genuine third path have you not treated as real, including doing nothing?
Do not evaluate it yet.
The load-bearing assumption
Which single belief would change the decision if it proved wrong?
Untested constraints
Which deadlines, budgets or stakeholder positions are verified, and which are assumed?
The evidence map
What is given, derived, inferred or unknown? Keep approximations visible.
Renewal notice
Treated as fixed
Set two years ago
Current licence cost
Rosters are rebuilt weekly
About 15 hours a week are lost to manual fixes
Some turnover traces to roster chaos
Whether award compliance is exposed
Verify the extension, stabilise the shift rules, then choose tooling against those rules.
Confirm whether an award-compliance exposure already exists. If it does, the timing and scope of the next step change.
Stop here. Framing prepares a decision; it does not make the decision.
No options were scored. Nothing was recommended. The question became the right one - which is the point.
